problemStatement: Tool approval behavior is spread across request creation, direct user decisions, Chat turn continuation, new-turn auto-denial, Generation run completion, message-part projection, and Tool invocation projection in convex/chatRuntime.ts. The current direct decision mutations are last-write-wins, so a later conflicting click or retry can make the stored request disagree with the client response or with already-projected durable state. The extraction must improve locality without weakening three distinct authorization shapes or duplicating the accepted Generation run lifecycle rules.
solutionSummary: Introduce a mutation-scoped Tool approval lifecycle module with five caller-first operations: request, recordDecision, hasPendingForRun, applyContinuation, and denyPendingForNewTurn. Preserve current behavior while migrating all lifecycle-related reads and writes, then make decisions first-write-wins in one small behavior patch: same-outcome retries are idempotent and retain the original reason, while opposite outcomes fail. Keep Generation run transition legality in the existing pure lifecycle module, keep general Tool invocation recording outside the new module, and use MutationCtx directly rather than inventing a storage port. Document the prepare-only atomic ordering of auto-denial and the same-transaction continuation-target claim in the interface and CONTEXT.md.
currentStateAnalysis: convex/chatRuntime.ts currently owns applyApprovalResponseToParts, resolveCanonicalApprovalDecision, denyPendingApprovalsForChat, applyApprovalResponses, createToolApprovalRequestForChat, approveToolCall, denyToolCall, and the markGenerationRunCompletedForChat pending-request query. The direct mutations patch approved or denied unconditionally; applyApprovalResponses later treats the stored row as canonical and can reject the entire prepare transaction if it no longer matches the client response. denyPendingApprovalsForChat intentionally does not project an old run's terminal state to the chat because both callers are inside prepareGenerationForChat and atomically claim the status slot for the imminent replacement run. applyApprovalResponses temporarily marks the continuation message streaming before prepare binds it to the new run, but Convex transaction atomicity prevents that intermediate state from becoming externally visible. recordToolInvocationsForChat also reads toolApprovalRequests only to validate a foreign-key-like linkage; it remains outside the lifecycle module because general Tool invocation recording is explicitly not lifecycle ownership.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: No new external system or runtime capability is introduced. All work runs inside existing Convex mutations using the same database, indexes, authentication context, and Next.js-to-Convex calls already used by the Durable turn runtime.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The browser records a user decision through approveToolCall or denyToolCall and then appends the same approval response to the AI SDK message; the next POST /api/chat request carries that response into Durable turn runtime and prepareGeneration. This gameplan does not change request fields, Convex mutation arguments, schema validators, AI SDK ToolUIPart shapes, or stored status literals. The new module must preserve the current producer/consumer sequence while making the stored decision immutable after its first resolution.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: All lifecycle writes stay within the caller's Convex transaction, so linkage errors, canonical-decision mismatches, opposite re-decisions, or later prepare failures roll back the full mutation. Missing and cross-user decision targets retain the indistinguishable `Approval not found` error; pending and expired continuation errors retain their existing messages; an opposite re-decision adds stable `Approval already resolved`. The browser already records the local response only after the mutation succeeds and already surfaces failures through the existing toast, so no new UI recovery path is required.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: Convex retries mutations transactionally. approvalId remains the request idempotency key: exact request replays are no-ops and linkage collisions fail. Decision resolution becomes first-write-wins under transaction retry: pending may transition once to approved or denied; a same-outcome retry returns success without changing resolvedAt, resolvedByUserId, or reason; an opposite outcome fails. Continuation groups responses by paused Generation run and sends one approvals-resolved signal per run; new-turn closure groups pending requests and relies on the Generation run lifecycle to ignore already-terminal races.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: No schema or data migration is required; existing pending, approved, denied, and expired rows remain valid. Reverting the gameplan restores the old implementation and last-write-wins behavior without unreadable data, although reverting after relying on first-write-wins would re-open the race rather than require a backfill. The gameplan should therefore be reverted as a unit if necessary; no compensating data write is needed.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: No feature flag. Patch 2 is a behavior-preserving extraction and Patch 3 is a narrow correctness hardening at the canonical decision write. Running old and new decision semantics simultaneously would make concurrency behavior depend on which call path executed and would defeat the invariant.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Patch 1 adds pending interface-level test stubs. Patch 2 introduces the deep module, shared Generation run status projection helper, and all behavior-preserving caller migrations, then implements the extraction tests. Patch 3 enables first-write-wins, implements the decision-race tests, and records the accepted Tool approval lifecycle vocabulary. The dependency graph is sequential because Patch 3 must change the single decision implementation introduced by Patch 2.

contextResources.why: These files define the current five lifecycle touchpoints, direct decision flow, stored table/index shapes, continuation response extraction, UI success-before-local-update order, and same-transaction prepare behavior that the extraction must preserve.

The Generation run lifecycle remains the sole authority for approval-requested, approvals-resolved, abort, first-terminal-wins, and message status transition legality. The Tool approval lifecycle may gather facts and apply verdicts but may not duplicate this table.

Request creation is run-owned, continuation and new-turn closure are chat-owned, and direct approve/deny mutations are self-identity-match. The module receives verified authority facts and must not collapse these shapes into a caller-constructible union.

These suites encode late-Stop handling, all-approved/any-denied continuation, cumulative message-part projection, auto-denial cascades, completion pending checks, durable prepare sequencing, and client mutation-before-local-response behavior.
Defines pre-launch schema policy, security/auth expectations, architecture vocabulary, scope verification, and the requirement to record a newly accepted deep module in the domain glossary.

acceptanceCriteria: convex/domain/tool_approval_lifecycle.ts exports a mutation-scoped factory with exactly the five approved operations: request, recordDecision, hasPendingForRun, applyContinuation, and denyPendingForNewTurn.

The request operation preserves approvalId idempotency, full run/message linkage validation, late-settled-run no-op behavior, request insertion ordering, awaiting message/run writes, and guarded chat status projection.
markGenerationRunCompletedForChat obtains hasPendingApprovals through hasPendingForRun after its existing early terminal guard and no longer queries toolApprovalRequests directly.
recordDecision preserves the self-identity-match authorization shape and the indistinguishable `Approval not found` result for missing and cross-user rows.
A pending decision transitions once to approved or denied; same-outcome retries do not alter reason, resolvedAt, or resolvedByUserId; opposite-outcome retries fail with `Approval already resolved`.

applyContinuation treats stored decisions as canonical, cumulatively rewrites multiple responses on one message, projects matching Tool invocations, sends one approvals-resolved signal per prior Generation run, and never repaints a run already settled by Stop.
applyContinuation returns a narrow ContinuationTarget and documents that prepareGenerationForChat must bind it to the imminent Generation run within the same Convex transaction before commit.

denyPendingForNewTurn owns the fixed `auto-denied: new generation started` reason, closes only the authenticated owner's pending requests and related nonterminal state, and documents that it is prepare-only and must be followed by the replacement run's status-slot claim in the same transaction.
Regeneration target/version validation still occurs before auto-denial, so a stale regeneration request cannot destroy valid pending approvals.

projectRunStatusToChat has one shared implementation consumed by existing terminal writers and Tool approval request creation; the pure Generation run lifecycle remains free of MutationCtx and database access.

recordToolInvocationsForChat remains outside the lifecycle module and retains only its narrow approval-link validation read; the plan does not claim general Tool invocation persistence as Tool approval lifecycle ownership.
The public Convex mutation names, validators, return compatibility, stored schema, AI SDK message shapes, and Durable turn runtime wire calls remain backward-compatible.
CONTEXT.md records Tool approval lifecycle only after the implementation and focused tests pass.

Focused Vitest suites, TypeScript checking for touched modules, Biome checks for touched files, git diff --check, intended-path diff review, and final git status all pass without modifying unrelated files.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Use the caller-first five-operation interface rather than a generic event union.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The operations represent genuinely different authorization facts, timing, return values, and lifecycle outcomes. A generic command union would make invalid authority combinations representable and force callers to learn implementation vocabulary.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Make Tool approval decisions first-write-wins, including the reason and resolution metadata.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Last-write-wins can make durable state disagree with the client response before continuation or with already-projected message and Tool invocation state after continuation. Convex transaction retry makes immutable resolution deterministic.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Use MutationCtx directly and do not introduce a ToolApprovalStore port.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Convex is the single production persistence adapter and the existing in-memory MutationCtx is already the local test stand-in. A new port would re-declare generated database behavior without a second production adapter.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Keep Generation run transition legality in generation_run_lifecycle.ts and share only the guarded database projection helper.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The accepted lifecycle table already owns approval-requested, approvals-resolved, abort, and race rules. The new module should gather approval facts and apply verdicts, not create a competing transition table.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Keep denyPendingForNewTurn prepare-only instead of adding an independent old-run chat projection.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Both valid callers atomically create and claim a replacement run in the same Convex transaction; any later failure rolls back the denial. A standalone close operation would have different projection semantics and should be introduced only with a real caller.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Keep general Tool invocation recording outside the Tool approval lifecycle even though it validates an approval request link.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Recording inputs, outputs, step numbers, and terminal results is Tool invocation behavior. Its narrow referential lookup does not make it an owner of approval decision or lifecycle transitions.
The expired schema literal has no producer. Adding an expiry operation before a real caller exists would widen the interface with hypothetical behavior.
